title: Secret capability intent
description: Diamond Standard (founder 2026-09-01; extended 2026-09-08 on the founder's 'we need to standardise, dont like these half baked inconsistent solutions'). 'This workload needs a credential called HF_TOKEN, and a vendor gives it to us' is the agent's absolute limit. Which vault holds it, which store reads it, which bootstrapper is allowed to write it and how the register records it are the compiler's, from the founder's DNA. There is no field for a vault, a store, a provider, a region or a secret value on purpose -- a value in an intent would be a secret in git (LAW 21).

workload.description: the workload that reads it; the compiler places the ExternalSecret where that workload runs

origin.description: vendor: a third party issues it and bin/idp-bootstrap-vendors writes it into the vault once. generated: no third party, so the estate mints it -- the compiler emits the random_password and the vault entry, and no human ever sees the value (R52).

rotation_days.description: recorded on the vault entry and in the register; a credential with no stated life is one nobody rotates

key.description: the name the workload reads it under; Kyverno refuses a secret in an env var (platform/edge/kyverno-secrets-policy.yaml), so the compiled Secret is mounted and read as <KEY>_FILE
